# Clicking to close the end-of-turn ledger selects the card below

## Problem statement

Pressing an action button on the end-of-turn ledger (the **Turn Summary** dialog — `[ Next Turn ]`, and by extension `[ Bank Loan ]`) also selects the hand card rendered underneath it. Closing the ledger should only resume the deferred closing; it must leave the hand untouched.

## Users

- **The human player, at the end of every day** — has just reviewed their P&L statement and presses `[ Next Turn ]` to start the next day.
  - *As a player closing the end-of-turn ledger, I want the hand to be exactly as I left it, so that I do not start the next day with an accidental card selection or an unexpected "placing from hand" state.*
- **A player who ends the day with a full hand** — the hand row is directly under the ledger's action row, so this is the common case, not an edge case.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Pressing `[ Next Turn ]` on the Turn Summary dialog dismisses the ledger and starts the next day **without** selecting, highlighting, or entering a "placing from hand" / "event selected" state for any hand card (`pendingHandIndex` stays `null`, `uiPhase` returns to `market`, and no card is bought, moved, played, or discarded).
- Pressing `[ Bank Loan ]` (enabled) opens the mid-game loan selector and likewise never changes hand-card selection; cancelling back to the summary leaves the hand untouched.
- The fix holds when the ledger's action button geometrically overlaps a hand card (the normal layout: the middle hand card sits directly under `[ Next Turn ]`), and for both mouse and touch input.
- A regression test reproduces the defect in a real Phaser scene: it positions a hand card under the ledger's action button, dispatches a real pointer press/release at the button, asserts the closing resumes (or the loan selector opens) **and** asserts the hand-card selection state is unchanged.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Closing the end-of-turn ledger no longer selects a hand card, so every new day starts with a clean hand and no accidental placement state.

## Constraints

- The Turn Summary dialog is the only gate in front of the deferred closing: `[ Next Turn ]` must remain the sole way to resume it, and the enabled/disabled `[ Bank Loan ]` matrix, tab switching and keyboard navigation must keep working exactly as today.
- Overlay-pattern compliance (AGENTS.md UI best practices): `createOverlayBackground` / `createOverlayButton` from `@ui`, all elements parented into `s.hudContainer`, depths 199 (backdrop) / 200 (box) / 201 (elements), everything tracked in `s.overlayObjects`, instant appearance (no fade — reduced-motion safe).
- The fix must not weaken the deliberate click-through protections elsewhere (tutorial tooltip DOMElement isolation, `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`) or the drag-drop click-vs-drag thresholds.
- No new engine/state semantics: this is a presentation/input bug; the closing economy and ledger figures must be untouched.
- Reduced-motion, replay/headless and competitive paths must keep their current pacing and behaviour.

## Existing state

- The Turn Summary dialog is rendered by `presentTurnSummaryPanel()` in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`. The panel is `PANEL_WIDTH = 680` × `PANEL_HEIGHT = 640`, centred on the 1280×720 scene (`panelY ≈ 40`, bottom ≈ 680).
- Its action row sits at `btnY = panelY + PANEL_H - 62 ≈ 618`, with `[ Next Turn ]` at `centerX - 120 ≈ (520, 618)` and `[ Bank Loan ]` at `centerX + 120 ≈ (760, 618)`.
- The hand row is centred on `columnCenterX ≈ 467` with `handY ≈ 628` and `handCardH = 80`, so hand cards span roughly y 590–666 and x 251–683 (three 140 px cards at ≈ 319 / 467 / 615). **`[ Next Turn ]` therefore sits directly over the middle hand card.**
- The action buttons act on `pointerdown` (`nextTurnBtn.on('pointerdown', …)` → `dismissPanel()` then `handlers.onNextTurn()`). The hand's business/upgrade cards act on `pointerup` in the drag-drop path (`container.on('pointerup', …)` → `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`), and the closing's `advanceTurn` starts the next day only after a bounded wait (`s.time.delayedCall(800, …)` or the bounded income-collection deferral).
- Working hypothesis to confirm during implementation: the button's `pointerdown` destroys the button and the full-screen input-blocking backdrop, so the matching `pointerup` hit-tests against the now-uncovered hand card beneath and its click-to-select handler fires. Because the button overlaps the card, this is repeatable for the common full-hand case.
- Related work already shipped: the tabbed P&L Turn Summary (`MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY`), the turn-summary gate (`MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R`), the bank-loan button (`MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7`), and the tutorial tooltip click-through fix (`CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV`).

## Desired change

- Make the ledger's action buttons consume the complete press/release cycle so a `[ Next Turn ]` / `[ Bank Loan ]` press can never be interpreted as a hand-card click, even when the button overlaps the hand row.
- Alternatively (or additionally), ensure the hand layer cannot receive pointer events while the Turn Summary overlay is presented — without blocking the overlay's own controls.
- Keep the ledger's layout, values, tab strip, keyboard navigation and the `[ Next Turn ]`-only resume contract unchanged.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the reported control is `[ Next Turn ]` in the Turn Summary dialog (the "end-of-turn ledger"); the same renderer serves the competitive panel, so the fix must cover both.
- **Risk — over-blocking:** a blunt "disable the hand layer while any overlay is up" change could break legitimate hand interactions after dismissal, or the drag-drop manager's registered draggables. Prefer a scoped guard that only suppresses hand clicks during the ledger's own press, and restore it on dismissal.
- **Risk — button responsiveness:** moving the action buttons from `pointerdown` to `pointerup` would change the press feel and could interact with the drag thresholds; if chosen, cover it with the existing dialog browser tests.
- **Risk — layout regression:** shrinking or moving the panel to avoid the hand row must keep every statement line, the tab strip and the `[ Bank Loan ]` hint on-screen at 1280×720 (and the reduced-motion/instant-appearance contract).
- **Scope-creep guard:** anything beyond "the ledger's action must not select a hand card" (e.g. a general overlay-input audit, or tooltip behaviour in the ledger — `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO`) is a separate work item, not this fix.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts` — the dialog renderer: action buttons (`[ Next Turn ]`, `[ Bank Loan ]`), dismissal, overlay objects; the primary fix site.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `presentTurnSummaryGate()` / `advanceTurn()` / `finishTurnPresentation()`; the closing that the button resumes.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — hand-card `pointerup` click handlers (`onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick`) and the drag-drop registration; the leaked event's destination.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` — `onHandBusinessCardClick` / `onHandUpgradeCardClick` / `onHandEventCardClick` and their `uiPhase` gates.
- `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts` / `core/src/ui/OverlayButton.ts` — shared backdrop/button factories and their input behaviour.
- `core/src/ui/HandView.ts` — hand layout (card positions) and interactive card sprites.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-dialog.browser.test.ts` — existing overlay browser coverage to extend.
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-gate.test.ts` — existing gate coverage.
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — Turn Summary dialog + closing gate documentation (update the interaction contract).

## Related work

- `MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41` — End of Turn summary dialog (parent epic; completed).
- `MS-0MW4XULA90002OEY` — Turn summary as a P&L statement (completed).
- `MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R` — Turn Summary gate (completed).
- `MS-0MVXYCICT0051LU7` / `MS-0MVXYCJCK006UE62` — Bank Loan button and its enabled/disabled matrix (completed).
- `MS-0MUWD9C1A004JZVQ` — Refactor end-of-turn presentation (completed).
- `MS-0MV767QTO008JUDJ` — Clicking a selected hand card deselects it (completed; same selection state).
- `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` — Tooltips in the end-of-turn ledger (open; same dialog).
- `CG-0MSTB03U6009J2WV` — Tutorial tooltip pointer pass-through fix (completed; same class of click-through defect).
- Repository docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (Turn Summary dialog + closing gate), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `core/docs/DEVELOPER.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- No clarifying questions were needed. The seed report ("When I click on the button to close the end of turn ledger, the card in my hand below the button is selected. It should not be.") identifies the dialog (the Turn Summary / end-of-turn ledger), the trigger (its action button) and the defect (hand-card selection) unambiguously, and repo research resolved the rest.
- Q: "Which control is 'the button to close the end of turn ledger'?" — Answer (agent research): the `[ Next Turn ]` button in the Turn Summary dialog (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummaryOverlay.ts`). Evidence: `MS-0MW6GZKZZ006PLLO` uses "end-of-turn ledger" to mean the Turn Summary dialog; the dialog's only close/resume control is `[ Next Turn ]`.
- Q: "Is the defect a layout overlap or an input-handling leak?" — Answer (agent research, to be confirmed during implementation): both are present — the action row geometrically overlaps the middle hand card, and the button dismisses the overlay on `pointerdown` so the matching `pointerup` can reach the hand card. Evidence: computed panel/hand geometry and the `pointerdown` / `pointerup` handlers above.
- Assumption (documented): the primary target is single-player play; the competitive per-seat panel uses the same renderer and `[ Next Turn ]` button, so the fix should cover it too.

# Intake brief — Cards should represent the actual income and reputation changes

## Problem statement

During play, the income and reputation figures shown on a placed business or community-space card are derived from the card's static values plus any upgrade bonus (`baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`). They ignore the modifiers the engine actually credits — board synergy, the same-type adjacency penalty, the duplicate-business (market-saturation) factor, and staff bonuses. A card can therefore display `+161` while the player is credited a different amount, so the card text contradicts the game economy and misleads placement and staffing decisions.

## Users

- **Players** who plan placements, upgrades and staff hires from the numbers shown on their cards.
  - "As a player, I want a placed card's text to show the income and reputation it actually generates, so I can make placement and staffing decisions without guessing."
  - "As a player, when I place a synergy neighbour or employ a Chef, I want the card's numbers to update immediately, so I can see the effect of my decision."

## Acceptance Criteria

- Placed business/community-space cards show the **effective per-turn income total** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy + duplicate factor + staff bonuses) in the on-card cash line, equal to the per-slot amount the engine credits.
- Placed cards show the **effective per-turn reputation total** (base + upgrade bonus + synergy) in the on-card reputation text, equal to the engine's per-slot reputation credit.
- Hover tooltips for placed street cards, hand cards and market cards show the same effective totals **and break them down** into base plus each modifier (upgrade, synergy, duplicate factor, staff), so no display surface shows stale base-only figures for a placed card.
- Every instance of a card, wherever it is displayed (a street slot, the hand, the market or any future surface), shows the modified income and reputation — never base-only figures — on the card face and in every hover tooltip.
- Staff bonuses are included in the displayed values on demand (read-only) without mutating the `currentIncome` / `currentReputationPerTurn` caches, reusing the same computation path as `applyIncome` so the displayed text can never disagree with the credited amount.
- Tests cover a plain card, a card with a synergy neighbour, a card with an employed staff bonus (own and adjacent), and a duplicate-saturated card, asserting the on-card total and the tooltip breakdown equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Players will be able to trust the income and reputation numbers on their cards: the card shows the coins and reputation actually credited each turn, and the tooltip explains how that total is built, so placement and staffing decisions are informed by real values rather than static base figures.

## Constraints

- The adjacency caches (`currentIncome`, `currentReputationPerTurn`) are read-only during display; staff buffs must be recomputed on demand, per the caching-safety contract documented in `MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`.
- Display computation must share the engine's source of truth (`computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs`, `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`) so display and credit can never diverge.
- Rendering runs per card per refresh, so avoid expensive recomputation beyond what the engine already does each turn; memoise or cache per-slot effective values if needed.
- Baked SVG card faces (`generateCardSvgFromCsvRow` and the static assets) currently show no income/reputation text; the fix is in the Phaser overlay/tooltip layer, not the SVG faces.
- Reduced-motion, replay and headless modes must remain visually and behaviourally unchanged.

## Existing state

- **On-card income/reputation:** `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec()` (`src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`) computes `totalIncome = baseIncome + incomeBonus` and `totalReputation = reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`. These are rendered by `applyUpgradeOverlays()` on street, hand and market cards.
- **Street hover tooltip:** built inline in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` as `Income: +${baseIncome + incomeBonus}/turn`, with reputation from `reputationPerTurn + reputationBonus`.
- **Hand/market hover tooltip:** `buildCardTooltipInfo()` in `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` uses the same base + bonus formula.
- **Actual values:** `card.currentIncome` = base + upgrade + synergy + duplicate factor (set by `syncCardCurrentIncome` / `recalculateCard` in `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`); `card.currentReputationPerTurn` = base reputation + upgrade bonus + synergy reputation. Staff buffs are deliberately **not** cached and are applied read-only in `applyIncome()` via `computeBusinessStaffBuffs()` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs()`.
- `generateBusinessCardSvg()` also uses base + bonus but is test-only (not on the production render path).

## Desired change

Make every card display surface show the modified values for that card instance wherever it appears: the card face shows the effective **total**, and the tooltip shows the total plus a **base + modifier breakdown**. Staff bonuses are included on demand, there is no location-based exception (hand, market and street instances all show modified values), and the adjacency caches are left untouched.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — accept/extract effective income and reputation totals (needs grid/staff context or precomputed per-slot values).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — pass per-slot effective values into the overlay spec and update the street tooltip text with the breakdown.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — `buildCardTooltipInfo()` (and any street tooltip builder) use effective totals plus the base/modifier breakdown for placed cards.
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — expose a read-only per-slot effective income/reputation helper (total plus base/modifier components) reusing `computeBusinessIncome`, `computeBusinessStaffBuffs` and `computePerBusinessSkillBuffs`.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — existing staff buff helpers (consumed read-only; never mutated).
- `src/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `getIncomeResult()` preview path, if it should also agree with the effective values.
- `tests/main-street/` — new/updated tests asserting on-card totals and tooltip breakdowns equal the engine's per-slot credited amounts.

## Related work

- **MS-0MV8LHN0W0017XU1** – Reputation bonuses should have no delay between businesses (completed).
- **MS-0MVRDGNFU001DDQW** – Park should give a good reputation bonus (completed).
- **MS-0MUVB2ZES005V83Y** – AI should not use Community Favour as much (completed).
- **MS-0MW0UCMF9004H9NT** – Single-player income: duplicate-factor applied to `computeBusinessIncome` / `syncCardCurrentIncome` (completed) — establishes the cached `currentIncome` values this item should display.
- **MS-0MVYG50V1007W8BP** – Reduced income for duplicate businesses (completed) — the duplicate-factor link surface.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "card text" means the on-card income/reputation overlay plus the hover tooltip. The baked SVG face shows no income/reputation today, so it is out of scope.
- **Confirmed (producer):** both surfaces are in scope; the card shows the effective total and the tooltip shows the breakdown into base and modifiers; staff bonuses are included.
- **Confirmed (producer, plan session):** *all* instances of a card, regardless of location (street, hand, market), show the modified data in both the card face and the tooltip — there is no unplaced-card exception.
- **Risk:** duplicating the income computation could drift from `applyIncome`; mitigate by extracting one shared read-only per-slot helper that returns both the total and its components.
- **Risk:** recomputing staff buffs per render could cost performance on large streets; mitigate with per-slot memoisation keyed on the turn/state revision.
- **Scope creep:** showing animated deltas on each card as bonuses change is a separate enhancement; record as linked work items rather than expanding this item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q:** Which surfaces must be in scope — the on-card overlay text, the hover tooltips, or both? — **Answer (producer):** Both; the tooltip breaks the value down into base and modifiers. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** both, so the card and its tooltip never contradict each other.
- **Q:** Should the displayed income include staff bonuses (on-demand) or only the cached adjacency/synergy/duplicate effects? — **Answer (producer):** Include staff bonuses. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** include staff bonuses, so the text matches the income actually credited.
- **Q:** Should the card show only the effective total, or also a breakdown of base / synergy / staff contributions? — **Answer (producer):** The card shows the total; the tooltip shows the breakdown. Source: interactive reply. **Recommended option:** effective total on the card, with the breakdown in the tooltip.

### Plan session (2026-11-08)

- Q: How should we reconcile parent AC3 ("hover tooltips for placed street cards, hand cards and market cards") with AC4 ("unplaced cards continue to show base + upgrade")?
  A (producer, plan session): "All instance of a card, regardless of their location in the game, should include the modified data in both the card and the tooltip." There is no unplaced-card exception.
  Final: **producer answer supersedes the earlier conservative reading.** AC4 rewritten to require modified values for every card instance wherever displayed; the overlay, tooltip, helper and integration-test children were revised to match.
- Q: None further — the intake appendix already resolved the scope decisions (both surfaces in scope, staff bonuses included, effective total on the card, breakdown in the tooltip).
  Final: intake answers stand unchanged.

## Plan

Six child tasks, test-first order:

1. **MS-0MW84013K0020ACZ** — Test: effective income/reputation helper returns correct totals and components
2. **MS-0MW84ALYG0065AWM** — Implement: read-only effective income/reputation helper with component breakdown
3. **MS-0MW843ARF0060F2K** — Implement: wire effective totals into card overlay spec
4. **MS-0MW843BSS0020R1B** — Implement: wire effective totals and breakdown into tooltips
5. **MS-0MW843CTF001WOCH** — Tests: on-card overlay and tooltip integration tests
6. **MS-0MW843DQQ00132PD** — Documentation: update code comments and docs

**Revision (producer clarification):** every card instance, in any location, shows the modified data on both the card and the tooltip. The former "unplaced cards keep base + upgrade" rule is retired, and children 1–6 were rewritten accordingly.

**Documented assumption for the no-slot case:** a hand or market instance has no board position, so position-dependent modifiers (adjacency synergy, same-type adjacency penalty, slot-bound staff buffs) evaluate to zero, while the upgrade bonus and the duplicate/saturation factor for its business type still apply — all resolved through the same shared helper, never a second formula. The instance is not counted twice when deriving its own saturation factor.

# Assistant — verify documented staff effect (staff-assistant)

## Goal
Confirm that `staff-assistant` (Assistant, management-company) is properly defined — card data, parsed typed field, description text and docs — and that it behaves exactly as documented, by adding or tightening a behavioural test that asserts its documented effect and scope. This card is one of 26 per-card verification children under the parent audit epic `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND`.

## Documented effect (authoritative: GDD Appendix D.4)

- **Ability:** +2 hand slots
- **Scope:** player hand capacity (street-wide)
- **Backing data:** handSlotsAdded=2
- **Engine consumer:** maxHandSize (WeekStart / AiStrategy)

1. **Definition verified.** `staff-assistant` in `src/card-data.csv` carries the documented backing data (handSlotsAdded=2), the `description` text states the same effect at the same magnitude using the ×100 consistency rule, and `docs/game/card-catalog.md` / `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` agree.

Players who hire the Assistant can rely on its printed ability (+2 hand slots, scope: player) actually happening.

# Player hired staff, staff went to an AI business

**Score:** 0
**Rank:** new item (no parent)
**Type:** bug — **Pri:** critical

## Problem statement

In competitive play the street grid is shared and owner-tagged, but the staff employment paths never consult slot ownership: a walk-on staff applicant can be targeted at (and hired into) an AI opponent's business, and staff relocation can also move a player's member onto an opponent's business. The player pays the salary while the opponent's business gains the staff buff — the player's own hire silently strengthens a competitor.

## Users

- **Human player in competitive mode** — hires a walk-on staff applicant (or relocates a member) and expects the member to work *their* business.
  - As a competitive player, when a walk-on applicant appears I want them to walk into one of **my** businesses with a free employment slot, so that hiring them benefits me.
  - As a competitive player, when I relocate a staff member I want only my own businesses offered as destinations, so that I cannot accidentally staff an opponent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A walk-on staff applicant in competitive play is only ever targeted at a street slot the acting seat owns (`getSlotOwnerId(state, slot) === (state.activePlayerId ?? 0)`), and only when that business has a free employment slot. When the acting seat owns no business with a free slot, no applicant appears (the roll still consumes the day's trigger, exactly as the existing "no eligible business" behaviour).
- `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` and `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` reject a destination business the acting seat does not own, using the shared `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` gate (same `That business belongs to <seat>.` message as upgrades/sell/close); single-player is unchanged because `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent.
- Every employment write path (`hireStaffApplicant`, `placeStaffOnBusiness`, `moveStaffOnBusiness`) defensively refuses to employ a member at a business the acting seat does not own, throwing an error naming the real owner — so a UI/AI/headless caller can never persist the invalid state even if it skips the legality helper.
- Applicant trigger chance and the applicant business-type match pool consider only the acting seat's own businesses (`computeApplicantChance`, `hasEligibleBusiness`, and the type-gate pool in `resolveStaffApplicant`), so an opponent's businesses neither raise the player's applicant chance nor unlock a specialist applicant the player cannot employ.
- A save already carrying player staff employed at another seat's business is repaired on load: the member is released from that business (employment cleared, removed from `employedStaff`, logged in the activity log), remains the player's hired staff, and the repair is idempotent across repeated load/save round-trips.
- New deterministic automated tests cover the owned/unowned matrix — applicant targeting, applicant chance, placement, relocation, the type-match pool, and the save-repair path — built on `tests/main-street/helpers/competitive-fixtures.ts` (`buildHumanVsAis`) plus existing single-player staff fixtures, and run through the test skill.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments (`MainStreetEngineCommands`, `MainStreetAdjacencyOwner`, `MainStreetStateSerialize` JSDoc), `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` (hire/relocate rule now states placement is restricted to the acting seat's own businesses), `docs/game/card-catalog.md` (shared staff rules sentence), and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A competitive player can hire and relocate staff knowing the member works for them — their hire can no longer silently strengthen an AI opponent's business.

## Constraints

- **Single-player must be untouched.** `ownerTaggedGrid` is absent in single-player, so the ownership gate is a no-op there; all existing single-player staff behaviour, tests and Monte Carlo runs must keep passing unchanged.
- **One ownership predicate.** Do not invent a second ownership check: `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` / `getSlotOwnerId` (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts`) is the single source of truth and the established idiom for every other cross-owner mutation (upgrade, sell, close, upgrade highlights).
- **Determinism preserved.** Applicant resolution consumes `state.rng`; the fix must not add or reorder RNG draws in ways that change single-player seeded outcomes, and tests must be seeded rather than flaky.
- **No new scope.** Staff salary model, the 1-action relocation cost, the two-type staff model (management-company vs business staff) and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged.
- Save-format change (if any) must remain backward compatible: older saves without owner tags load unchanged.

## Existing state

- Shared, owner-tagged street: `state.ownerTaggedGrid` + `getSlotOwnerId` / `canActiveSeatActOnSlot` (`src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts:26`, `:161`). Every other cross-owner mutation already gates on it (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:313/571/619/769/849`, `src/MainStreetMarketSell.ts`, `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:174/318`, `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererDragDrop.ts:159/252`).
- Applicant resolution: `resolveStaffApplicant` → `hasEligibleBusiness` / `pickTargetSlot` / `computeApplicantChance` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1200-1360`) iterate the whole shared grid, with no ownership filter, so `pendingApplicant.targetSlotIndex` can be an AI business. `hireStaffApplicant` (`:1362`) then stamps `employedAtSlot = targetSlotIndex` and pushes onto that business's `employedStaff` with no ownership check.
- Placement/relocation: `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`:962`) checks hired-ness, business-staff type, business-type match and free capacity — but **not** ownership; `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1043`) delegates to it. `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`:1106`) and `moveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1073`) write the employment from those checks only.
- Market-row hires (`purchaseStaffCard`, `src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1059`) never place a member, and `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) has no live UI caller, so the applicant path is the one that can auto-place today; relocation is the other writer.
- Player-facing relocation UI derives destinations from `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` `buildMoveStaffAffordance` ~`:603`, used by the Manage-Card dialog and `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:393`), so it currently offers opponent businesses as legal destinations.

# Staff go to business or management company

## Problem statement

Hiring a **business staff** card (e.g. the Delivery Driver, `staff-delivery`) from the general market row does not set `employedAtSlot`, so the two-type model's runtime test (`isBusinessStaffCard` = "has an `employedAtSlot`") classifies the member as **management-company staff**. The member then appears in the management-company roster and Staff Pile, its business-scope effect is inert, its salary is still charged, and there is no way to correct it — the roster offers only *Lay off*, never *Assign to a business*. The player reported exactly this: a hired Delivery Driver "went to the management company" even though its card type is *Business*, and clicking it offered no way to assign it to an appropriate business.

**Chosen model (producer decisions Q1/Q2/Q3).** Business-staff cards are hired **unassigned** into the player's staff pool (the Staff Pile) — there is **no** hire-time destination step; the member receives no business-scope benefits until it is employed, while its salary costs remain. The player assigns an unassigned business-staff member to a business afterwards by clicking it / its roster row (*Assign to business*). The docs that currently promise hire-time placement are updated to describe this assign-later model. Roster and Staff-Pile classification is corrected so unassigned business staff are never shown as management-company staff, and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff so balance runs stop silently wasting hires.

## Users

- **Human player (single-player)** — hires a business-staff card from the market row; the member joins the staff pool unassigned and is assigned by the player via the staff surface.
  - As a player, when I hire a Delivery Driver I want to click it afterwards and assign it to one of my Food/Commerce businesses, so that its adjacency purchase discount actually applies.
  - As a player, when an unassigned business-staff member has no matching business yet, I want to see it labelled as *unassigned business staff* (not management company), with costs and benefits behaving accordingly, so I know I must either build a matching business or lay the member off.
- **Human player (competitive)** — the same flow, restricted to the businesses their seat owns.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Business-staff hire is unchanged and unassigned is first-class. Hiring a business-staff card (`staffCardScope(card) === 'business'`) from the general market row joins the player's staff pool with **no** `employedAtSlot` and **no** hire-time destination step (Q1-B). An unassigned business-staff member receives no business-scope benefits while its salary is still charged (Q2-B); management-company staff hire is unchanged.
- *Assign to business* affordance. From the staff-management surface (the roster overlay opened from the Staff Pile / a member click), an unassigned business-staff member offers an *Assign to business* action; the player picks a destination that satisfies the existing placement predicate (`canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`: business-type match via `staffMatchesBusiness`, free employment slot via `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, competitive ownership via `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). The assignment is executed through `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` — initial placement of an unassigned member stays action-free, a later move of an employed member stays 1 action — and is undoable and logged.
- No legal destination is handled gracefully. When no business the acting seat may employ at matches the member's `allowedBusinessTypes` with a free slot, the member simply remains unassigned (Q2-B): the assign action reports the reason (e.g. "no matching business with a free employment slot") and spends nothing; the member keeps appearing as unassigned business staff until a legal destination exists or it is laid off.
- Roster and type surfaces classify by card type (Q3-A). The management-company roster and Staff Pile list management-company staff only; unassigned business staff are surfaced as an explicit *unassigned business staff* group with the assign affordance and are never presented as management-company staff; employed business staff appear on their business (Manage Card) as today. Effect semantics keyed on `employedAtSlot` are unchanged.
- Lay-off stays available for unassigned business staff. Dismissal of an unassigned business-staff member works from the staff surface with the same quoted cost (one turn's salary + the salary-scaled reputation cost) as other doors.
- Single-player AI / Monte-Carlo hires place business staff (Q3-A). In AI-driven play (Monte Carlo / auto-play), a business-staff hire places the member at a legal destination business as part of the hire; when no legal destination exists the hire action is not taken, so an AI hire is never silently inert. The competitive AI remains staff-free (unchanged).
- Deterministic automated tests cover the matrix: business-staff hire → unassigned for the human player; the assign affordance's legality matrix (type match / no match / no free slot / opponent-owned destination in competitive / no owned business at all); assign is action-free on initial placement and 1 action on relocation; undo/redo and save/load round-trips; roster and Staff-Pile classification (management-company vs unassigned business staff); AI hire-and-place and AI skip-when-no-destination; management-company hire unchanged — seeded and run through the test skill.
- Documentation updated (Q1-B: "update GDD if necessary"). The hire-flow wording in `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` (D.4) is updated to the assign-later model (currently they promise "hiring business staff chooses the destination business"); code comments, JSDoc, README and any relevant wiki/docs entries are updated too.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A player who hires a business-staff card (such as the Delivery Driver) can click the member afterwards and assign it to the business it works at, so the hire actually does what the card promises — until then it is honestly labelled *unassigned business staff* with its costs, rather than masquerading as a management-company employee.

## Constraints

- **One placement predicate.** Destination legality must reuse `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (and therefore `staffMatchesBusiness`, `hasFreeEmploymentSlot`, `canActiveSeatActOnSlot`). Do not add a second business-type or ownership check.
- **No hire-time placement step.** Per Q1-B the market-row hire flow is unchanged; the fix is the assign affordance and the classification/doc corrections, not a `placing-staff` phase at hire.
- **Effect semantics stay keyed on `employedAtSlot`.** An unassigned business-staff member's business-scope skills remain inert (the existing scope gate); classification changes affect *display surfaces and AI behaviour*, not buff resolution.
- **Action economy unchanged.** Hire is 1 action; assigning an unassigned member (initial placement) is free; relocating an employed member stays 1 action (`isStaffRelocation`); management-company staff are never placed or relocated.
- **Determinism preserved.** AI/enumeration and applicant-resolution changes must not add or reorder `state.rng` draws in a way that changes seeded outcomes (Monte Carlo baselines may shift only as the intended Q3-A consequence, and must stay seeded/deterministic).
- **Single-player untouched where it should be.** The competitive ownership gate stays a no-op without `ownerTaggedGrid`; existing single-player behaviour passes.
- **No new scope.** Staff salaries, the two-type effect model, the applicant flow and the AI's staff-free competitive strategy are unchanged; extra opportunities (e.g. rebalancing staff salaries) are recorded as linked work items, not folded in here.
- **Backward-compatible saves.** Loads must tolerate older saves that contain unassigned business staff.

## Existing state

- **Hire path never places.** `purchaseStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1061`) deducts coins, removes the row card and pushes `{ ...card }` into `state.staffCards` (`:1085`) with **no** `employedAtSlot`; `hireStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:904`) simply delegates to it. `canPurchaseStaff` (`src/MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts:1043`) only checks presence and coins — never business availability (this is now the chosen behaviour for the player, per Q2-B).
- **UI hires immediately.** `onStaffCardClick` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts:785`) validates with `canPurchaseStaff` and executes `hireStaffCardCommand` (`:827`) with no destination step — retained as-is under Q1-B.
- **The engine already knows the card is business staff.** `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:996`) gates on `staffCardScope(member) === 'management-company'` (`:1014`), and `staffCardScope` (`src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts:147`) falls back to the template marker for an unplaced card — so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *business* staff to the engine, and `placeStaffOnBusiness` can already place it.
- **The roster uses a different test.** `isBusinessStaffCard` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:248`) is `employedAtSlot !== undefined`, so an unplaced Delivery Driver is *management-company* staff to every roster/tooltip surface: `buildCompanyRoster` (`src/MainStreetRoster.ts:93`), `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts:262`) and `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:701`). That is the visible contradiction ("listed as a business staff member" but sitting in the management company).
- **Effects are inert, salary is not.** Business-scope buffs resolve from `business.employedStaff` (`src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`, `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts`), so an unplaced member contributes nothing, while `applyStaffOngoingCosts` still charges its salary — the behaviour the producer confirmed as intended (Q2-B).
- **No assign door today.** `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts:1906`) offers only [Confirm lay-off]; business rows appear only in the Manage Card once the member is already employed (`buildBusinessStaffRows`, `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts:74`); `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:1091`) rejects an unplaced member (`employedAtSlot == null`) and `buildMoveStaffAffordance` (`src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts:632`) therefore never offers it. `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:922`) is the correct action-free initial-placement command but has **no live UI caller**.
- **Docs promise the superseded model.** `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md:509` and `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md:544` state that hiring business staff "also chooses the destination business — its initial placement is free and part of the hire action"; under Q1-B this wording is updated to the assign-later model (in scope).
- **Single-player AI hires without placing.** `enumerateLegalActions` (`src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts:837-860`) offers `hire-staff` for any affordable, not-already-employed staff card, with no placement step, so a Monte-Carlo AI hire of business staff is inert (Q3-A fixes this).
- **Tests.** `tests/main-street/staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts` asserts that hiring *management-company* staff never assigns a destination; `staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts` covers the coin/hand mechanics only; no test covers the assign-affordance flow or roster classification of unassigned business staff.

## Desired change

1. Keep the market-row hire exactly as it is (Q1-B): business staff join unassigned; no destination step.
2. Add the *Assign to business* interaction for unassigned business-staff members: an affordance on the staff surface (roster overlay / member click), a destination picker derived from `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness`, executed via `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (action-free initial placement), undoable and logged.
3. Correct the classification surfaces (Q3-A): `buildCompanyRoster`, `selectManagementCompanyStaff`-driven displays and `buildStaffPileTooltip` must not present business-staff members as management-company staff; an explicit *unassigned business staff* group/row with the assign affordance (and lay-off) is added.
4. Align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path (Q3-A): business-staff hires place the member at a legal destination as part of the hire, or the hire is skipped when none exists.
5. Update the rules/GDD/catalogue docs to the assign-later model (Q1-B "update GDD if necessary").
6. Cover the matrix with deterministic tests; keep saves backward compatible (unassigned members load unchanged and remain assignable — no silent place/delete/reclassify).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetRoster.ts` — `buildCompanyRoster` (`:93`) classifies by `staffCardScope`; an *unassigned business staff* group with assign affordance data (reuse the `buildMoveStaffAffordance`-style destination derivation, but accepting unplaced members).
- `src/MainStreetBusinessStaff.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — display classification for unassigned members; `selectManagementCompanyStaff` (`:262`) / `isBusinessStaffCard` (`:248`) usage split between display and effects.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showCompanyRosterDialog` (`:1906`) gains an *unassigned business staff* section with [ Assign to business ] (and [ Lay off ]); the assign destination picker flow.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — `buildStaffPileTooltip` (`:701`) excludes unassigned business staff; an assign affordance builder (`buildAssignStaffAffordance`) listing legal destinations for an unplaced member.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts` / `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — assign flow wiring (destination-pick phase or reuse of `moving-staff` with an accept-unplaced predicate); `onMoveStaffClick` (`:362`) / `canMoveStaffOnBusiness` (`:1091`) boundary.
- `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` (`:922`) is the assignment command (may need an unplaced-member legality path; `canPlaceStaffOnBusiness` already accepts one).
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `enumerateLegalActions` (`:837`) hire-staff for business staff carries/requires a legal destination slot (hire-and-place composite), skipped when none; `executeAction` handling.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `MainStreetMarketPurchase.ts` — any legality tweaks to expose the assign action and confirm `placeStaffOnBusiness` handles the unplaced member (it already does via `staffCardScope`).
- `tests/main-street/staff-general-market-purchase.test.ts`, `staff-two-type-redesign.test.ts`, `staff-placement-commands.test.ts`, `company-roster.test.ts`, `staff-pile.test.ts`, `staff-movement.test.ts`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts`-based fixtures — new assign-flow, classification, save/load and AI hire-and-place coverage.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `docs/game/card-catalog.md`, `docs/game/the-build-gdd.md` — hire-flow wording updated to the assign-later model.

## Related work

- `MS-0MW3JXF6U00753LB` — *Implement two-type staff redesign deltas in card data and engine* (introduced the business/management-company split and the `staffCardScope` marker).
- `MS-0MW4MSNMJ006E9JH` — *add skill scope classification and type-consistent assignment* (the scope gate that makes an unassigned business-staff skill inert).
- `MS-0MWC1T8K2000DWZA` — *Company roster overlay: view and lay off management-company staff* (the roster this member wrongly appears in; the surface gaining the assign affordance).
- `MS-0MWC9PB24000BEUM` / `MS-0MWCB35QG0030XU6` — *Roster model* / *Manage Card: staff rows and per-row move* (the row/move patterns to reuse).
- `MS-0MWBB146L005SU31` — *Player hired staff, staff went to AI business* (the sibling ownership bug in the same hire/placement area; established the save-repair precedent and the ownership predicate).
- `MS-0MUOSUKUC004G2VO` / `MS-0MUOSUNYR0073SI1` — *staff movement* / *gate relocation with 1 action* (`placeStaffOnBusinessCommand` and `isStaffRelocation`).
- `MS-0MW6HEBP80070YND` — *Staff effects are not implemented* (open; the inert-effect symptom overlaps but is a separate defect).
- Earlier staff-placement work: `MS-0MU3BTSQ8006ZRCU` (placement engine/commands), `MS-0MTIOLY2A0092OT1` (per-business `allowedBusinessTypes` / `employedStaff`), `CG-0MT4WXNR80090FXZ` (specialization applicants), `CG-0MSTOATDU006UGAX` (walk-on applicant flow).

## Assumptions & decisions (producer confirmed)

- **D1 — Q1 answered (b): post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only.** No hire-time destination picker; the market-row hire flow is unchanged (member joins unassigned). The GDD/core-rules/catalogue wording that currently promises hire-time placement is updated to the assign-later model (in scope, per the producer's "update GDD if necessary"). The producer's phrase "hire goes to the hand" is read as *joins the staff pool / Staff Pile*: staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55) — if the producer intended the card hand instead, that is a much larger scope change and should be raised at planning.
- **D2 — Q2 answered (b): hire proceeds unassigned, benefits not received, costs remain.** When a business-staff hire has no legal destination, the hire is not refused; the member stays unassigned, its business-scope effects are inert, and its salary is still charged. The assign action surfaces the reason and spends nothing.
- **D3 — Q3 answered (a): both.** Roster/Staff-Pile classification is corrected (unassigned business staff shown as *unassigned business staff*, never management-company), and the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path places business staff at a legal destination or skips the hire (competitive AI stays staff-free).
- **A4 — No silent save repair.** Unlike the competitive cross-seat repair (`MS-0MWBCX7MS00960BH`), an unassigned business-staff member is *not* silently placed on load — the player assigns it (or it stays unassigned until they do).
- **A5 — Scope is classification + assign UI + AI hire placement + docs.** No salary, effect-strength, tier or card-data changes; any such opportunity is a linked follow-up item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (fix shape): How should a business-staff hire get onto a business?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — post-hire *Assign to business* affordance only (hire unassigned, assign later); update GDD if necessary." Decision recorded as **D1**. Interpretation note: the producer's follow-up "hire goes to the hand" is treated as *the staff pool / Staff Pile*, because staff cards are never moved to the card hand by engine design (`moveToHand` rejects staff, CG-0MT3KZNQB0053K55; `staff-general-market-state.test.ts`). If the producer intended the card hand, that must be raised at planning as a scope change.
- **Q2 (no legal destination): When a business-staff hire has no matching business with a free slot, what should happen?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(b) — the hire goes through as unassigned; benefits are not received (effects inert until employed) and costs remain (salary charged)." Decision recorded as **D2**.
- **Q3 (scope): Should the fix also correct roster classification and align the single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire path?** — Answer (producer rgardler, interactive reply): "(a) — both: roster classification correction and single-player AI/Monte-Carlo hire alignment." Decision recorded as **D3**.
- **Q: Which hire path produced the reported Delivery Driver?** — Answer (agent, evidence): the general market row (`onStaffCardClick` → `hireStaffCardCommand` → `hireStaffCard` → `purchaseStaffCard`), which is the only non-applicant hire path and never assigns `employedAtSlot`. The walk-on applicant path does place business staff (`hireStaffApplicant` sets `employedAtSlot = pending.targetSlotIndex`). Source: repo inspection.
- **Q: Is the Delivery Driver business staff or management-company staff?** — Answer (agent, evidence): business staff. `src/card-data.csv` ships `handSlotsAdded` and `actionsPerTurn` empty and `allowedBusinessTypes = Food|Commerce`, so `staffCardScope` returns `'business'`; `docs/game/card-catalog.md` classifies its Type as `Business`. The runtime only *downgrades* it to management-company because `employedAtSlot` is absent. Source: repo inspection.

## Problem statement

The competitive HUD scoreboard draws each seat's row label in that seat's raw persisted colour (`row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR`). The colour-blind-safe palette deliberately includes the Okabe–Ito black (`#000000`), so a seat assigned that hue renders an unreadable label on the dark HUD bar. The same defect was already fixed for the Turn Summary tab strip (MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ) by the shared `ensureReadableSeatColour()` helper; the HUD simply never adopted it.

## Users

- **Competitive player** — can read every rival's coin/reputation/score row on the scoreboard regardless of which palette colour a seat was dealt.
- **Single-player player** — unaffected; no roster means no per-seat rows are drawn.

Example user story:

- As a competitive player, when a seat is dealt the palette's black, I can still read that seat's scoreboard row so I can track their totals.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A competitive HUD scoreboard row whose seat colour falls below WCAG AA contrast against the HUD background is lightened toward white via `ensureReadableSeatColour()`, so the row label is always readable.
- The HUD passes the actual HUD bar background as the contrast backdrop (not merely the dialog-panel default), so the check matches the surface the text sits on.
- A seat colour that already clears the ratio is drawn unchanged (the exact caller string), preserving seat identity.
- The existing neutral fallback (`NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR`, used only for a malformed/absent seat colour) is preserved.
- Unit/browser coverage pins the black-seat case on the HUD: a seat dealt `#000000` renders a label that clears WCAG AA against the HUD background, while a legible seat keeps its exact hue.
- All existing tests pass.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

No competitive player loses a scoreboard row to an unreadable seat colour.

## Constraints

- Presentation-only: resolve the text colour for rendering; do not mutate persisted `PlayerRecord.colour`, consume RNG, or add a persisted field.
- Reuse, don't fork: `ensureReadableSeatColour()` and its colour maths in `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` remain the single source of legibility truth (same helper as the Turn Summary tab strip).
- UK English spelling in comments, tests and docs.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — `renderCompetitiveScoreboard()` builds rows from `buildCompetitiveScoreboard()` and sets the Phaser text `color` to `row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR` (currently `#ffffff`) with no contrast adjustment.
- `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` — already exports `ensureReadableSeatColour(seatColour, backgroundHex = DIALOG_PANEL_BACKGROUND, minContrast = MIN_SEAT_TEXT_CONTRAST)`, plus `parseHexColour`, `contrastRatio`, `mixTowardWhite`, `toHexColour`. It lightens a too-dark colour toward white in 20 steps until it clears WCAG AA (4.5:1); a colour that already clears the ratio is returned unchanged.
- The HUD bar is drawn as `s.add.rectangle(hudLeft, hudY, hudWidth, HUD_BAR_HEIGHT_PX, PANEL_FILL, PANEL_FILL_ALPHA)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`, where `PANEL_FILL = 0x1a1408` and `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA = 0.85` (a very dark brown, not pure black). The row text is drawn above the bar at `hudY - HUD_BAR_HEIGHT_PX / 2 - HUD_SEAT_ROW_OFFSET_PX`.
- Existing test file `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` asserts each row is drawn in its persisted colour; that assertion must be reconciled with the new legibility rule (legible seats unchanged, illegible seats lightened).

## Desired change

1. In `renderCompetitiveScoreboard()`, resolve the row text colour through `ensureReadableSeatColour(row.colour ?? NEUTRAL_ROW_COLOUR, <HUD bar background>)` instead of using the raw seat colour.
2. Pass the real HUD bar background (the `PANEL_FILL` hex, e.g. `#1a1408`) as the backdrop argument so the contrast threshold matches the drawn surface.
3. Extend `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` with a black-seat legibility case and keep the "legible seat keeps its exact hue" assertion.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererCompetitiveHud.ts` — resolve the row text colour through `ensureReadableSeatColour()`
- `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts` — existing shared helper (no change expected; reference only)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — `PANEL_FILL` / `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA` HUD bar background constants
- `tests/main-street/competitive-hud-colour.test.ts` — extend with the legibility case

## Related work

- **MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ** — Turn summary shows a true summary tab (completed): discovered-from parent; its audit-rejection fix introduced `ensureReadableSeatColour()` for the tab strip and filed this HUD follow-up.
- Related docs: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (competitive HUD / scoreboard sections).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Backdrop choice (low).** Passing the real HUD bar colour (`#1a1408`) rather than the dialog default slightly changes which hues are lightened. Mitigation: pass the HUD constant and pin the black-seat case in tests.
- **Test reconciliation (low).** The existing "renders each seat in its persisted colour" test will now be false for an illegible hue. Mitigation: keep the exact-hue assertion for legible seats and add an explicit lightened-hue assertion for black.
- **Scope creep.** Any broader seat-colour legibility audit (e.g. placed-card borders) is out of scope and becomes a linked work item.
- **Assumption.** The black palette entry is the only palette colour that fails AA against the HUD bar; the helper handles any future addition generically.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

No producer interview was required: the seed context (filed as `discovered-from:MS-0MWBWRITL0089GGJ`), the existing shared helper and the referenced renderer/tests were sufficient to draft the brief. The one implementation nuance worth recording was resolved by repo inspection:

- Q: Which background should `ensureReadableSeatColour()` compare against on the HUD? — Answer (agent, researched): the **HUD bar fill**, `PANEL_FILL = 0x1a1408` at `PANEL_FILL_ALPHA = 0.85` (`src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts`, drawn in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts`), not merely the dialog-panel default `DIALOG_PANEL_BACKGROUND = '#000000'`. Recorded in the ACs and Desired change. Source: repo inspection of `MainStreetRendererHud.ts` / `MainStreetConstants.ts` / `MainStreetSeatColours.ts`.
- Q: Does the fix require changing the shared helper? — Answer (agent, researched): no; `ensureReadableSeatColour()` already supports an explicit `backgroundHex`, so this is a call-site change plus tests. Source: `src/MainStreetSeatColours.ts`.

# Model: owner-filtered expense breakdown derivation

## Goal

Generalise the single-player per-card expense breakdown so it can be derived for
one owner, giving competitive seats the same per-card detail from the seat's own
committed state.

Parent: `MS-0MWBZDVCH008P8X5` — *Per-card expense breakdowns on competitive Turn Summary seats*.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`; make `expenseLineBreakdown(state,
  category)` delegate to it so single-player output is unchanged.
- Staff source: the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` when a roster exists,
  else the shared `state.staffCards` (single-player / hand-built states).
- Community-space and business source: `state.streetGrid` filtered by
  `getSlotOwnerId(state, i) === ownerId`, sold slots excluded.
- Street reduction: the owner's `getStreetScopeSkills(owner.staffCards)` for
  staff and `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` for community/business,
  mirroring `applyCompetitiveOngoingCosts` (`hostReduction`).
- Keep the existing item shape (`name`, `coins`, `base`, `modifiers`) and the
  invariant `base + sum(modifiers) === coins`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner(state, ownerId, category)` derives per-card expense breakdown items for one owner, and the existing single-player `expenseLineBreakdown(state, category)` delegates to it so single-player breakdown output is unchanged.
- Staff breakdown items for a competitive seat come from that owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards`, with `coins` from `computeStaffSalaryCost(getSalaryScopeSkills(card), card.ongoingCost)`, `base` = `-card.ongoingCost` and every named modifier (e.g. Operations Manager) with its signed amount.
- Community spaces and business costs breakdown items list each owned space/business on its own line with its base ongoing cost, derived from the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` via `getSlotOwnerId`, excluding sold slots and synthesising no modifiers.
- The street-wide reduction is computed from the same skill set the engine uses per category: the owner's `getStreetScopeSkills(players[ownerId].staffCards)` for staff and `getEmployedSpecializationSkills(state)` for community spaces and businesses.
- Absent-safe: an unknown owner, a roster-less or hand-built state, or an empty source yields no breakdown (`{}`) rather than an empty item list or a throw.
- The per-card breakdown for competitive seats uses the same data sources and reconciliation as single-player: derived from the owner's `players[ownerId].staffCards` for staff and the owner-filtered `state.streetGrid` for community spaces and businesses, never invented or synthesised.
- Presentational and pure: deriving a breakdown mutates no state, consumes no RNG and needs no engine change.

## Impact

A single pure helper can now explain any owner's expense category from that owner's own committed cards, which is what the competitive panel needs.

## Key Files:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts` — `expenseLineBreakdown`, new `expenseLineBreakdownForOwner`, `streetReduction`
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` — `computeStaffSalaryCost`, `computeStaffSalaryDiscount`, `getSalaryScopeSkills`, `getStreetScopeSkills`, `getEmployedSpecializationSkills` (read-only reuse)
- `src/MainStreetAdjacencyOwner.ts` — `getSlotOwnerId` (read-only reuse)
- `tests/main-street/turn-summary-tooltips.test.ts` — the assertions this child makes pass

## Goal

Make the Turn Summary's Business costs breakdown reconcile to the committed
total when a business employs a Bookkeeper: today the tooltip's per-business
items use the card's raw `ongoingCost` while the engine charges the
Bookkeeper-reduced cost, so the difference is presented as a coin clamp.

## Evidence

- `applyBusinessOngoingCosts` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`) charges
  `effectiveBusinessOngoingCost(state, i, cost)` — the slot's own
  `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` (Bookkeeper, −20%) applied before the
  street-wide Cost Cutter reduction.
- `expenseLineBreakdown` (`src/scenes/MainStreetTurnSummary.ts`) builds each
  business item from `(slot as BusinessCard).ongoingCost` with no per-business
  reduction, so `sum(items) + streetReduction` exceeds the committed line when a

- Business expense breakdown items expose the Bookkeeper's per-business reduction as a named modifier (`base + sum(modifiers) === coins`), using `computeBusinessOngoingCostReductionPct` and the same helpers the engine charges with.
- The breakdown reconciles exactly to the committed business total for a state with an employed Bookkeeper, with no spurious clamp line in the tooltip.

- Deterministic tests cover a Bookkeeper-reduced business in both modes, added to the existing tooltip suites and run through the test skill.
- Presentational only: no engine change, no state mutation, no RNG, no new localisable copy beyond the existing `t()` keys.

A player who hires a Bookkeeper sees the discount named in the Business costs tooltip instead of a phantom "coins available" clamp.
